stories.title: British healthcare worker with Ebola evacuated from DR Congo to UK
bullet_points: Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit  A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed.
“A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday.
“The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.”   Continue reading...

bullet_points: Conservation officers say more than one bear may have been involved in attack on women near their home  Search teams in  Canada  have discovered the body of a 20-year-old woman and confirmed that both she and her mother were killed in an attack that conservation officers now believe could have involved multiple grizzly bears.
Late on Tuesday, conservation officers in British Columbia said the two women, who were reported missing over the weekend, were located near a trail a short distance from their home.

stories.title: ANC faces anger over poor services as South Africans vote in local elections
bullet_points: Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts  The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure.
The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party.
However, polls showed it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the  last municipal elections  in 2021 and 40.2% in  2024’s national elections .

stories.title: Egypt fines prominent editor Lina Attalah and shuts independent news outlet Mada Masr
bullet_points: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website  Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country.
Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt.

stories.title: One dead and another missing in suspected grizzly bear attack in Canada
bullet_points: The incident took place in the same province where a grizzly attacked a group of schoolchildren last November  A mother is dead and her daughter is missing in western Canada after a suspected grizzly bear attack in the same community where a bear  attacked a group of schoolchildren  earlier in the year.

On Tuesday, the British Columbia conservation officer service said in a social media post that it had launched a search for the two missing people on the weekend, and that during the search on Sunday an officer found the mother’s body.
The search for her 19-year-old daughter is ongoing.

Brazil, the host of  last year’s UN climate conference , set out the world’s first global “roadmap” for phasing out fossil fuels on Tuesday, showing that countries could boost their economies and pull people out of poverty while breaking the link with coal, oil and gas.
